newsitem.title: USA: Rawlings Sporting stock off on lower Q1.
newsitem.headline: Rawlings Sporting stock off on lower Q1.

text.p: Shares of Rawlings Sporting Goods Co fell more than two points after the company revised fiscal first-quarter revenue and profit expectations.

Rawlings said first quarter revenues and net income will fall below year-ago levels and the sluggish revenues will result in an unspecified loss in the first quarter, which ends November 30. The company reported earnings of $890,000 in the first quarter of 1995 on revenues of $35.5 million.

"For one thing, Rawlings' shipments are being delayed," said Wesley Roberts, an analyst at Hilliard Lyons. "Unlike in previous years, customers are ordering goods on an as-needed or just-in-time basis. The first quarter used to be a solid sales period for Rawlings because they shipped goods for the spring in November."
The St. Louis-based sporting goods manufacturer cited weakness in sales of commemorative baseballs, baseball gloves and basketballs as having the greatest impact on the first-quarter sales slump.
Roberts added that Rawlings could rebound in the second or third quarters as fill-in demand by retailers improves.
Shares of Rawlings were trading off two to 8-3/8.
